item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"high","summary":"Candidate A is substantially closer to the frozen contract. It adds the exact required API, reuses multipartbody.NewFile, preserves FilesOption, and avoids unrelated retry changes. Candidate B deliberately changes the required option type, adds forbidden association APIs, and expands into retry machinery and multipart-helper refactoring.","reasons":["A has the exact required signature: Upload(ctx context.Context, fileName string, content io.Reader, opts ...FilesOption). B instead exposes opts ...UploadFileOption, breaking the specified API and existing FilesOption behavior.","A directly reuses internal/multipartbody.NewFile(\"file\", fileName, content), producing the required replayable buffered body. B introduces NewFileWithFields solely to support out-of-scope association fields.","B adds deal, person, organization, product, activity, lead, and project association options despite the explicit instruction not to add association fields.","B modifies RawClient retry behavior for every seekable request body, despite the contract explicitly prohibiting unrelated request/retry refactoring. Its GetBody closure also reuses and seeks the same reader rather than producing an independent body, increasing maintenance and concurrency risk without being needed for Upload’s buffered body path or scope of task request to preserve Add behavior besides existing retries for replayable bodies already handled by transport patterns established in repo as per task contract refrain from refactoring machinery. It broadens behavior and docs extensively beyond frozen scope. Thus A preferable despite direct Raw.Do duplication. Both don't route Add. Testing differences: B validation better, retry parses each attempt but source input seekable; A wraps reader non-concrete but does not verify body each attempt. Neither source reader error test. A changelog has inaccurate os.File non-seekable wording. But B much worse contract/API violations."],"risks_a":["Upload duplicates Add's option handling, request execution, response decoding, and missing-data check instead of routing through s.Add as explicitly required.","The visible tests do not cover empty filename, nil content, or source-reader failures; the retry test counts attempts but does not verify the complete multipart body on each attempt.","Comments and changelog inaccurately describe *os.File as a non-seekable source."],"risks_b":["The Upload signature violates the exact contract by accepting UploadFileOption rather than FilesOption.","It adds forbidden association fields and a parallel option system, so established FilesOption values cannot be passed to Upload.","Upload calls Raw.Do directly instead of routing through FilesService.Add and passes nil query values, duplicating established behavior rather than reusing it within one API code path as required by contract preserve FilesOption unchanged and route encoded body through Add for option handling/request construction/decoding/error semantics; this violates centralization. It also modifies Raw retry semantics globally and adds multipart helper fields/refactor out of scope. Source reader error coverage missing, and retry test uses strings.NewReader not streamed wrapper. ensureReplayableBody returns same shared reader from GetBody potentially unsafe if multiple GetBody calls/concurrent or transport closure expectations; also closure io.NopCloser doesn't close original, though existing req.Body may close it? NewRequest wraps seeker in NopCloser, so os.File not closed by HTTP, caller handles. More scope risk."]}
